title: Honest Trends Over Time
objective: After this lesson you will be able to resample time series with declared granularity, handle gaps explicitly, index baselines for comparison, and reject dual-axis correlations.
why: Time plots lie by granularity (daily noise vs monthly signal), gaps (missing months silently connected), and scaling (dual axes manufacturing correlation). Honest trends declare granularity, flag gaps, and compare via indexed baselines — the same series tells opposite stories under different choices, so choices get stated, not hidden.

blocks.text: Daily (noise + events), weekly (patterns), monthly (trends): each answers different questions, and switching granularities reverses conclusions (Simpson-adjacent effects over time). Declare granularity with reason (weekly: weekday effects smoothed, events visible); show alternatives in appendix when stakes are high.

blocks.caption: Regularize with explicit gaps: absent weeks ≠ zero weeks

blocks.text: Comparing series of different scales: index both to 100 at start (relative change comparable) or panel separately with shared x. Dual y-axes let scaling choices manufacture any correlation — banned except with locked, justified scales (which is to say: effectively banned). Baselines make growth comparable honestly.

blocks.title: Calendar traps
blocks.text: Unequal months, 53-week years, holiday shifts, and timezone cutoffs all warp time comparisons — normalize periods (equal lengths, like-for-like holidays) before trending, and state the calendar rules beside the chart.

blocks.title: Resample the weeks
blocks.note: Run it: two populated weeks plus a missing Oct-12 week (absent, not zero). Gaps surface as missing entries — flagged downstream, never interpolated silently.

items: Declare granularity with reason; alternatives in appendix when stakes high
Missing periods absent (flagged), never zero-filled silently
Indexed baselines or shared-x panels; dual axes effectively banned

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice resampler and confirm weeks + gap. (b) Index two series (100→120, 50→65) to base 100 and state growth verdicts vs raw comparison. (c) Write the granularity note for a weekly revenue chart (why weekly, what daily would add/hide).
hints: Indexed: 120 vs 130 (second grew faster relatively) — raw gap (+20 vs +15) misleads; indexed compares growth honestly.
Weekly note: smooths weekday noise, keeps event visibility; daily adds noise/hides trend; monthly hides events.
exercise.why: Gap visibility (absent ≠ zero), indexed comparison (relative honesty), and granularity justification (reason + alternatives) are the three trend judgments.
exercise.code: // Trend-note pattern: granularity + gap policy + comparison basis, stated.

quiz.q: Missing October in a monthly series, line connects across. Fix?
options: Break the line + flag the gap: connected gaps fabricate continuity; absent periods display as absent
quiz.explain: Connected lines imply measured continuity. Gaps display as breaks with flags — honesty about missingness.

quiz.q: Ad spend vs sales dual-axis 'correlation'. Response?
options: Redraw indexed (=100) or paneled with shared x: dual scales manufacture correlation visually
quiz.explain: Independent y-scales make any two risers 'correlate'. Indexed/paneled views remove the scaling degree of freedom.

quiz.q: Daily noise obscures the quarterly question. Move?
options: Resample up (weekly/monthly) with declared granularity: match grain to question, appendix alternatives
quiz.explain: Grain follows question: quarterly questions need aggregated views. Declared resampling with alternatives beats secret smoothing.

summary: Declared granularity, flagged gaps, indexed comparisons, banned dual axes. Time honest by construction.
